# Agatha Sowerby

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker and community leader  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs. Agatha Sowerby  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Sowerby  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Agatha  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby is a stout, heavy woman whose gait is described as a perpetual waddle. Her physical presence is formidable and notable enough to be mentioned by her neighbors. In her later years, she requires spectacles, which she eventually replaces.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P19](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0019), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c30 P0](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0000), [v2 c6 P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014)_

## Personality

Mrs. Sowerby is an exceptionally proficient, opinionated, and observant homemaker who takes great pride in keeping her chores executed thoroughly and maintaining order. Highly vigilant, inquisitive, and prone to meddling, she keeps a close watch on her neighbors' lives and takes pride in speaking her mind freely without fear or partiality. Despite her sharp tongue, intrusive nature, and pessimistic, condemnatory initial reactions, she possesses a kindly, generous heart and a deep sense of neighborly duty. She holds firm, traditional religious and political beliefs, frequently offering unsolicited advice based on her strong convictions.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P21](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0021), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v1 c26 P3](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0003), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, where she keeps a keen watch over all passersby. A prominent community figure, she directs the local Sewing Circle, assists with the Sunday school, and acts as a pillar of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Obed Abernethy unexpectedly leaves town, her curiosity drives her to visit Grey Shutters, where Thirza Abernethy reveals that they are taking in an orphan child, an act Mrs. Agatha strongly condemns as risky. Upon meeting the orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, Mrs. Agatha bluntly criticizes her freckles and red hair, provoking Nell into a furious outburst. Though initially shocked, she forgives Nell after receiving a dramatic apology. Over time, Mrs. Agatha grows fond of Nell and takes interest in her progress at school and her community activities, such as the Village Improvement Society. Later, after her long-invalid husband Thomas Sowerby passes away, Mrs. Agatha faces financial difficulties due to an old mortgage on their farm.

## Background by volume

- Lived in Brierley at Sowerby's Hollow by a road through a ravine  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- Raised ten sons and daughters, and buried two  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030)</sub>
- Her husband's Boston employer once cheated him out of ten dollars  <sub>[v2 c1 P50](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0050)</sub>
- Had a childhood schoolmate whose red hair turned into auburn in maturity  <sub>[v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am utterly bewildered, indeed, and I shall not experience a single moment of mental or moral tranquility until I discover the reason for Obed Abernethy leaving Brierley this very day.  <sub>[v1 c1 P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005)</sub>

> A unfamiliar child is being brought into your house and home by you, and you are completely ignorant about him, his temperament, the kind of parents he possessed, or the manner in which he is apt to develop.  <sub>[v1 c1 P25](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0025)</sub>

> She’s awfully thin and plain, Thirza. Step over this way, child, so I can inspect you. Goodness gracious, has anyone ever witnessed such freckles? And hair that is as red as carrots!  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.  <sub>[v1 c13 P19](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0019)</sub>
